caption: A, mixed defaults, host off: the top row is “Default branches”, every repository is named with its branch, and engine’s fix/redirects stands out. The chip says where the pick leaves the rest.

B, the same pick: one section per repository. Engine shows its default, branches and the picked fix/redirects; frontend stays on main. The summary and the chip say “engine: fix/redirects · 4 on defaults”.

C, the same pick: the run board. Repositories expand in place on the left, and “Where each run starts” on the right says engine runs fix/redirects on localhost:4100 while the other four keep their defaults.
Shared main with GitLab connected: all five defaults agree, and pull requests appear with the repository they belong to. frontend’s !18 is picked; the other four stay on main.
One repository: the picker falls back to today’s shape — main, tasks, branches — with no repository names, grouping or summary to carry.
The way to connect from the footer: Connect GitLab… opens a dialog for gitlab.fnt.example, its host and a token. Connecting turns the host on and fills the pull requests in.
